<div class="wx-hero-inner">
  <p class="wx-eyebrow">Macroevolution · Macroecology · Conservation</p>
  <h1 class="wx-name">Wei Xu<span class="wx-cn">徐伟</span></h1>
  <p class="wx-role">Postdoctoral researcher, <strong>Tel Aviv University</strong>, Israel</p>
  <p class="wx-tagline">I study how Earth history, climate and traits build the biodiversity we see today &mdash; from Himalayan amphibians to Malagasy rainforest trees &mdash; and how that knowledge becomes conservation on the ground.</p>
  <ul class="wx-chips">
   <li>Phylogenetics</li><li>Biogeography</li><li>Diversity patterns</li>
   <li>Trait evolution</li><li>Mountains</li><li>Tropical rainforest</li>
   <li>Conservation planning</li>
  </ul>
</div>
</section>

<p class="wx-section-label">What I work on</p>

<div class="wx-grid">
  <div class="wx-card">
  <h3>Mountains as diversity engines</h3>
  <p>How uplift and climate history shaped the Himalaya, the Qinghai&ndash;Tibetan Plateau and the Hengduan Mountains &mdash; and why different vertebrate groups answered the same geology in different ways.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="wx-card">
  <h3>Large-scale conservation</h3>
  <p>Translating macroecological and phylogenetic evidence into conservation priorities at national and continental scale &mdash; as in our <em>PNAS</em> study revealing the hidden hotspots of amphibian biodiversity in China.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="wx-card">
  <h3>Trait diversity and evolution</h3>
  <p>How functional traits originate, diversify and drive radiations: frugivory-related traits across the global Annonaceae of tropical rainforests, and the trait innovations behind the worldwide radiation of modern toads.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="wx-card">
  <h3>Theory</h3>
  <p>Developing the conceptual side of macroevolution and macroecology &mdash; the theory that the tools should rest on. Work in progress; nothing published yet.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="wx-card">
  <h3>Software development</h3>
  <p>Building open tools for macroevolution and macroecology, starting with <a href="DataCode.html">BioGeoSyn</a> &mdash; making biogeographic inference reproducible and comparable across clades &mdash; with more to come.</p>
  </div>
</div>
